lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Ninety percent of the people who lived in the Western Hemisphere in fourteen ninety two were dead within about a hundred years.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Say that number out loud and most people picture soldiers, horses and steel.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: The record does not agree. Old World diseases, smallpox, measles, influenza, typhus, killed an estimated fifty six million people across the Americas by sixteen hundred. The pathogens moved faster than any army, or any rumor of one.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: They killed so many people, so fast, that the farmland they left behind grew back into forest, and the forest pulled enough carbon out of the air to show up in ice cores drilled in Antarctica today. That is not a metaphor. That is measured.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Columbus and the Columbian Exchange. Fourteen ninety two to fifteen fifty.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Columbus wades ashore on an island the Taino call Guanahani. He plants a flag and claims it for Ferdinand and Isabella of Spain.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: The Taino paddle out to greet the three ships. They bring cotton thread, parrots, and food. Gifts, not weapons.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Columbus writes it all down in his own diary, the same day.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Columbus, describing the people who had just fed him.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: They should be good servants and intelligent, for I observed that they quickly took in what was said to them, and I believe that they would easily be made Christians, as it appeared to me that they had no religion.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Two days later, on the next island, Columbus writes the sentence that finishes the thought.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: With fifty men they can all be subjugated and made to do what is required of them.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Before he sails on, he takes six Taino by force.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Fifteen thirteen. The Spanish Crown produces a text called the Requerimiento.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: It informs Indigenous peoples that the Pope has granted Spain their land, that the King of Castile is now their lord, and that refusal means war, enslavement, and the loss of their children.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: It is read aloud, in Spanish, by men in armor on horseback, to people who do not speak Spanish, sometimes from a distance at which no one could hear it at all. Then the attack begins.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Gonzalo Fernandez de Oviedo, the Crown's own chronicler, recorded that the jurist who drafted it, Juan Lopez de Palacios Rubios, laughed when told how it was used in the field.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: What that meant in practice: a legal formality that made conquest lawful on paper before a single sword was drawn, satisfied by reading words no listener understood.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Bartolome de las Casas, the Dominican friar who later spent his life fighting this system, called it unjust, impious, scandalous, irrational, and absurd.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: By fifteen twenty, smallpox has crossed the ocean and reached the mainland ahead of any Spanish army.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: It reaches Tenochtitlan before Cortes does. It kills the Aztec emperor Cuitlahuac within the year.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: It reaches the Inca Empire before Pizarro does. It kills the Sapa Inca, Huayna Capac, and triggers the civil war that Pizarro then exploits.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Two hemispheres had been separated for twelve thousand years, since the land bridge at Beringia went under water. The Old World had spent that time building a disease environment out of crowded cities and domesticated cattle, pigs, and horses. Indigenous Americans had none of the immunity that bought.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: The exchange runs in both directions. New World crops reach the Old World and rebuild it from the ground up.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: The potato, grown in the Andes for thousands of years, reaches Europe and grows in soil where wheat will not. Maize reaches West Africa by the fifteen fifties and becomes a staple crop across the continent. The tomato reaches Italy by fifteen fifty. Italian food as the world knows it today did not exist before this.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Tobacco builds the plantation economies of Virginia and the Carolinas. Sugar cane, an Old World crop planted in New World soil, creates a demand for labor that the Old World then fills from a third continent.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Fifteen forty five. The Spanish find a mountain of silver at Potosi, in what is now Bolivia.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: They adapt an Inca labor draft. Every adult man in the surrounding provinces owes four months a year underground, by candlelight, in tunnels where the temperature reaches forty degrees. Mercury used to extract the silver poisons the water and the workers.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: An estimated eight million people work Potosi over three centuries. It produces forty five thousand tons of silver, which funds the Spanish crown's wars in the Netherlands.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: And as the Taino die faster than they can be replaced on Hispaniola, the Spanish Crown authorizes a new labor source. Twelve and a half million enslaved Africans will be shipped across the Atlantic before the trade ends.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Five accounts of one exchange, and the first one was written to be believed by a king.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: In fourteen ninety three, Pope Alexander the Sixth draws a line one hundred leagues west of the Azores and gives Spain everything on the far side of it. He has never seen a map of what he is giving away.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Columbus's own letters read like a business proposal. He imposes a gold tribute on every Taino over fourteen. Those who fail to deliver it lose their hands.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: He writes to the Spanish court proposing to ship four thousand enslaved Taino to Seville every year, and he calculates the revenue himself.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: I could conquer the whole of them with fifty men and govern them as I pleased.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: That is Columbus, in a letter to Luis de Santangel, three months after he lands.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: The Taino have a word for the Spanish ships. Canoa. The same word for their own dugout canoes, scaled up to fit what they are seeing.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: A quarter of a million people lived on Hispaniola when Columbus arrived. Fewer than five hundred are left by fifteen forty eight.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: They do not go quietly. A cacique named Hatuey flees to Cuba with four hundred followers and organizes armed resistance. The Spanish catch him and burn him at the stake.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: A friar offers him baptism first, and tells him Christians go to heaven.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: I do not wish to go to Heaven. I do not wish to go where such cruel people might be.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: That is Hatuey, refusing.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Alfred Crosby publishes a book in nineteen seventy two that renames the whole event. Not a conquest. An exchange.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: The killing mechanism was not superior weapons. It was twelve thousand years of separation between two disease pools, and the Old World's pool was worse.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Alexander Koch and three other researchers measure it in a two thousand nineteen study. Enough farmland went abandoned, and enough forest grew back, that the carbon dioxide drop shows up in Antarctic ice as the lowest reading of the whole record, in sixteen ten.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: One later study puts the potato alone behind twenty five to twenty six percent of the Old World's population growth between seventeen hundred and nineteen hundred.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: The Columbian Exchange has been the most important event in human history since the end of the Ice Age.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Crosby wrote that in two thousand three, thirty years after he coined the term.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Immanuel Wallerstein argues in nineteen seventy four that modern capitalism was born between fourteen fifty and sixteen forty, and that it needed the Americas to be born.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Potosi is his clearest evidence. Eight million forced laborers. Forty five thousand tons of silver flowing through Seville, to Antwerp, to Amsterdam, funding the wars and the trading companies that follow.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Without that silver, he argues, there is no Amsterdam stock exchange in sixteen oh two, and no modern financial system built on the model it set.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: The essential feature of the modern world system is the axial division of labor between core and periphery.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: That is Wallerstein's own summary of the thing he spent a career describing.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: The first enslaved Africans reach Hispaniola in fifteen oh one, because the Taino are dying faster than the mines and the sugar fields can be worked.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Between fifteen oh one and eighteen sixty seven, twelve and a half million Africans are loaded onto ships bound for the Americas. An estimated one point eight million die during the crossing itself.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: On a Caribbean sugar plantation, life expectancy after arrival is seven years. Barbados alone imports three hundred eighty seven thousand enslaved Africans between sixteen twenty seven and eighteen oh seven.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: The knowledge came with the people too. Enslaved West Africans brought tidal rice cultivation techniques that built the rice economy of South Carolina and Georgia.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Eric Williams traced all of it forward, in nineteen forty four, from the plantation to the industrial economy that followed.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: The African slave trade and African slavery were the economic basis of the American Revolution.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: And here is what each account cannot hold at the same time as its own case.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: The Spanish imperial account leaves out the scale of the collapse it caused, ninety percent of a hemisphere, and the disease that did most of that killing.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: The Taino account does not separate what the sword did from what the microbe did. Both killed. The record does not always say which one, in which death.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: The ecological account leaves out the massacres, the enslavement, and the mutilations that happened alongside the disease, as if biology alone explains what people chose to do.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: The world systems account leaves out the person. It can describe eight million forced laborers as a labor supply and never once describe what that labor felt like from underneath.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: And the African diasporic account is the one most often left out of the other four, and it leaves out the African kingdoms and elites who were partners in the trade, not only its victims.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: By fifteen forty eight, fewer than five hundred Taino are left on Hispaniola. A quarter of a million people, gone in fifty six years.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: But a two thousand eighteen genetic study found that modern Puerto Ricans carry, on average, fourteen percent Indigenous ancestry.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: It survived through the bodies of women who had no say in the matter. They were not asked. They were not erased either.
